outline: 1162 Producing Equivalent Fractions using the Rule

examples.question_text:
Compare using $<$, $>$ or $=$.
a) $\frac{1}{5}$ and $\frac{1}{2}$
b) $\frac{1}{2}$ and one half
examples.solution_text:
a) Splitting the same whole into $5$ equal parts gives smaller parts than splitting it into $2$ equal parts.
$\frac{1}{5}<\frac{1}{2}$
b) $\frac{1}{2}$ is one of two equal parts, so it is one half.
$\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}$

examples.question_text: Which of $\frac{1}{4}$, $\frac{1}{6}$ and $\frac{1}{10}$ is closest to $\frac{1}{2}$? Explain your answer without using decimals.
examples.solution_text:
The smaller denominator gives the larger unit fraction.
$\frac{1}{10}<\frac{1}{6}<\frac{1}{4}<\frac{1}{2}$
All three are below a half. $\frac{1}{4}$ is the largest, so it is closest to a half.

examples.question_text: Which is the largest fraction: $\frac{1}{8}$, $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{1}{12}$ or $\frac{1}{3}$? Explain your answer.
examples.solution_text:
The smaller denominator gives the larger unit fraction of the same whole. Each other denominator is greater than $2$, so each other fraction is smaller than a half.
$\frac{1}{2}$ is the largest.
